detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with permission to search `index=azure`.
• Install and configure: Cloud posture integration via provider TA.
• Ensure `azure:monitor:activity` events are flowing (prerequisite UC: 4.10.1 when applicable).
• Map `azure` and field extractions per `docs/guides/aws.md`, `docs/guides/azure.md`, or `docs/guides/gcp.md` as appropriate.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure required cloud inputs per provider guide; index=azure sourcetype=azure:monitor:activity.
Expected sourcetype: `azure:monitor:activity`. Validate with:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="azure:monitor:activity" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="azure:monitor:activity"
| table _time action user resource
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
The search scopes `azure:monitor:activity` in `index=azure` and applies `*` to surface `Azure CSPM Misconfigured Workload Identity`. Tune time range and alert threshold to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare result counts to the vendor console (CloudTrail Event history, Azure Activity Log, GCP Logs Explorer, or service-native UI). Spot-check `_time` and actor fields. Confirm CIM acceleration only after TA field mappings are verified.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_10_18_alert` with appropriate severity. Dashboard: Dashboard panel, alert, and weekly compliance report..
Failure modes: (1) empty results — verify TA input and index routing; (2) duplicate events — check S3/SQS duplication; (3) missing fields — upgrade `Cloud posture integration via provider TA` and review `props.conf` aliases; (4) alert fatigue — add CMDB/allow-list exclusions documented in knownFalsePositives.
